name: SuperSplat
use_label: Edit 3D Gaussian splats in a browser
one_liner: A browser editor for inspecting, cleaning up and publishing 3D Gaussian Splats.

text.why: A Gaussian splat reconstructed from photographs arrives full of stray points and noise. SuperSplat opens that result, lets you delete what does not belong, line it up, shrink it and publish it — all in the browser, with nothing to download or install.
text.take: 3D tools usually start with a heavy install; this one starts with a URL, and takes you through to something you can show other people.
build: Built by PlayCanvas on web technology: a scene list, position/rotation/scale controls, several selection tools and a histogram of the splat data, all in one screen, with export and publish at the end. It is localised into several languages and can also be run locally from source.

who.role: People working with 3D scans, teams showing a space or product in 3D, and anyone teaching the subject.

start.text: Open superspl.at/editor and drag a Gaussian splat (.ply) file in.

caveat: It is for Gaussian splats, not a general 3D model editor (no obj/fbx workflow), and a large scene asks a lot of your machine’s graphics.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.
